claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to understand your family situation. Let me ask you about your child:

**How old is the child you're claiming for?** 

Please let me know:
- Is the child **under 16 years old**?
- Is the child **between 16 and 19 years old**?
- Is the child **20 years old or over**?

Also, if you have multiple children, please tell me about each of them so I can assess your eligibility for all of them.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 9 years old, so yes, he's under 16.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 9 years old (under 16), that's a good starting point. Now let me check the next eligibility requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about any work:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

(This is mainly relevant for older children, but I need to confirm for Alex's situation as well.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's only 9, so he's in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's clear - Alex is in school and not working, so that's no issue. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about benefits:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?** Specifically, I'm checking if he's receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit 

(At 9 years old, this is unlikely, but I need to confirm)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a regular 9-year-old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I'd expect. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news - this check is about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

(Again, at 9 years old this would be very unusual, but I need to check for completeness!)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, definitely not - he's only 9! He's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Ha! Fair point - I apologize for the obvious question! At 9 years old, Alex is clearly not in an apprenticeship. Let me move forward to the next important check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now we need to check an important requirement - your residency situation. This is crucial for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Can you tell me about where you normally live?** I need to check if you meet the UK residency requirements. Here are the main scenarios:

1. **Do you normally live in the UK?** (This is the most straightforward path)

2. Or do you have any of these special circumstances:
   - Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
   - Pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (with specific work, study, or job-seeking conditions)?
   - Are you a Crown servant living abroad in certain qualifying countries?

What's your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK - I live in Manchester with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's straightforward - you normally live in the UK, so you meet the residency requirement. Let me move on to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check responsibility for Alex:

**Are you responsible for Alex?** This means one of the following:

1. **You live with the child** - You live together in the same household
2. **You contribute to their upkeep** - You pay towards their care (food, clothes, housing, pocket money, etc.) at least at the level of Child Benefit
3. **You're paying maintenance** - You make payments under a court order or agreement towards the child's upkeep

Since you mentioned you live in Manchester with Alex, I assume you live with him - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You live with Alex, so you clearly meet the responsibility requirement. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good progress! Now I need to check something important:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** 

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent (or another family member) claiming Child Benefit for him?
- Or is Alex only being claimed by you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex - it's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Where does Alex live currently?** 

- Does he live with you at home in a normal living arrangement?
- Or is he in hospital?
- Or in care?
- Or in a fostering arrangement?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives at home with me in a normal living arrangement - nothing special like hospital or care or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's what I'd expect. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! We're nearly at the end. I just need to check one final thing:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you paying for his accommodation and upkeep yourself, without council support? (This is the typical situation, but I need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - I pay for everything myself. The council isn't paying for his accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's the final check complete. Let me now provide you with your eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ Great News! You're Eligible for Child Benefit

**Outcome: ELIGIBLE**

You **are eligible** to claim Child Benefit for **Alex**.

### Summary of Your Situation:
- **Child:** Alex (9 years old)
- **Relationship:** Lives with you at home in Manchester
- **Status:** In primary school, not working, no disqualifying benefits or apprenticeships
- **Residency:** You normally live in the UK
- **Funding:** You pay for his accommodation and maintenance
- **Other claimants:** None

### What This Means:
All the eligibility requirements are met for Alex, so you can proceed with claiming Child Benefit. 

### Next Steps:
1. **Apply online** at [www.gov.uk/child-benefit](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit)
2. You'll need to provide:
   - Your child's details (name, date of birth, National Insurance number if available)
   - Your details and National Insurance number
   - Bank account details for payments
   
3. **Processing time:** Claims usually take 6-8 weeks to process

### Support:
If you have any questions while applying, you can contact HMRC's Child Benefit helpline at **0300 200 3100**.

Is there anything else I can help you with regarding Child Benefit?
